introduction: On this second Sunday of Advent, Baruch calls Jerusalem to take off her robe of mourning, for God will lead his people home with joy. In the Gospel, the word of God comes to John the Baptist in the desert, and he proclaims: Prepare the way of the Lord; all flesh shall see the salvation of God. Paul is sure that God will complete the good work he has begun in us. Let us make straight the paths of our hearts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord has done great things for us. Let us bring him our prayers as we prepare his way.
intentions: For the Church: that she may prepare the way of the Lord by calling all people to repentance and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who mourn or live in exile: that God may clothe them in joy and bring them home. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose lives are crooked or rough: that they may find the straight path of conversion. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discouraged by their failures: that they may trust that God will complete the good work he began in them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that this Advent we may receive the sacrament of Reconciliation and prepare a place for Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way for your Son. Help us to make straight paths for him, and complete in us the good work you have begun. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Prepare the way of the Lord
reflection.body:
Luke begins his account of John the Baptist like a historian. He names the emperor, the governor, the local rulers and the high priests: "Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar..." Then he tells us where God's word actually came: not to the palace or the temple, but "to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness." God often speaks from the margins.

John preaches "the baptism of repentance for remission of sins," and Luke sees in him the voice Isaiah foretold: "Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight. Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low." Then comes the promise that reaches every person: "All flesh will see God's salvation."

Preparing the way means work: filling in the valleys of what is lacking in us, lowering the mountains of pride, straightening what is crooked. That is what conversion looks like.

Baruch adds a note of joy. He speaks to Jerusalem as to a grieving mother: "Take off the garment of your mourning and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God." Her children, once led away by enemies, are coming home, carried "with glory." God himself levels the mountains so that his people can return safely.

Paul gives us a word of confidence: "he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ." Our conversion is God's work before it is ours.

This week, ask yourself: what valley needs filling in my life, what mountain needs lowering, what path needs straightening? Bring it to God in the sacrament of Reconciliation before Christmas.
